headline_marked: [[Elon Musk gets FTC greenlight to buy Mesh Optical]] for critical AI interconnects
headline: Elon Musk gets FTC greenlight to buy Mesh Optical for critical AI interconnects
summary: The acquisition aims to tackle the "I/O wall" bottleneck in AI clusters, integrating optical networking into Musk's expanding AI infrastructure, including xAI and Terafab.
details: Elon Musk has received FTC approval to acquire Mesh Optical Technologies, an AI infrastructure startup specializing in light-based networking hardware for data centers. This regulatory green light, granted on June 25, clears the path for the deal, which is yet to be officially finalized.

Mesh Optical was founded by three former SpaceX employees who developed Starlink's optical communication links. This acquisition integrates optical interconnects, a technology critical for Musk's broader AI ambitions, including his semiconductor manufacturing facility and orbital data center factory.

The rapid growth of AI capabilities has shifted the primary challenge in scaling AI clusters from chip speed to data movement between processors. Current AI clusters, often comprising tens to hundreds of thousands of GPUs, require immense data exchange for training and inference tasks.

The industry faces an "I/O wall" where chip compute capacity outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Traditional copper interconnects have limitations at higher speeds and distances, leading to signal degradation and increased power consumption beyond short ranges.

Optical networking offers a solution by converting electrical signals into light for fiber transmission, enabling higher data volumes over longer distances with less power. This makes optical interconnects strategically vital for large-scale AI clusters, with companies racing to develop faster transceivers.

Musk's aggressive push into AI includes xAI, which deployed the Colossus supercomputer with over 200,000 Nvidia GPUs, and plans for Colossus 2 with a target of 1 million GPUs. He is also building Terafab, a multi-billion-dollar semiconductor manufacturing facility for AI chips.

headline_marked: Report: [[Apple interested in startup that runs giant AI models on iPhone]] without servers
headline: Report: Apple interested in startup that runs giant AI models on iPhone without servers
summary: The Information reports that Apple is reportedly looking into PrismML, a firm specializing in shrinking large AI models to run directly on devices, potentially bringing advanced AI capabilities to iPhones without cloud reliance.
details: Apple is reportedly exploring technology from PrismML, a startup focused on optimizing large AI models to run efficiently on mobile devices. This could enable advanced AI functionalities directly on iPhones, bypassing the need for constant server communication.

PrismML's approach aims to significantly reduce the computational footprint of sophisticated AI, allowing complex tasks to be processed locally. This would enhance user privacy and potentially improve response times for AI-driven features.

This reported interest signals Apple's strategic move towards more powerful on-device AI capabilities, aligning with its privacy-centric philosophy. It suggests a future where iPhones handle more complex AI tasks independently.
The development could lead to a new generation of intelligent features on Apple devices, from enhanced virtual assistants to more sophisticated photo and video processing, all powered by local AI.
